text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Scottish/Australian publisher of the "Melbourne Age", DAVID SYME, was born in 1827.
Australian pearling industry pioneer JAMES CLARK was born in 1857. He sold the "Star of the West" for 6,000 pounds, reputed to be the finest pearl ever found in Australian waters.

Indian leader MOHANDAS KARAMCHAND (MAHATMA) GANDHI was born in 1869. He used civil disobedience (non-violent non-cooperation) in his campaign for Indian independence, and was imprisoned several times by the British authorities.
He was assassinated on the 30th of January, 1948, in New Delhi, by Hindu fanatic NATHURAM GODSE.
The first Regimental Sergeant-Major at the Duntroon Military College in Canberra, HAROLD "The Marquis" CHUMLEIGH, was born in 1880.

American comedian and actor GROUCHO (JULIUS) MARX was born in 1890. His nickname came from his temper, and he was famous for his rasping voice, terrible puns and total amorality. He died on the 19th of August, 1977.
British comic CHARLIE DRAKE, who had a hit with "My Boomerang Won't Come Back", was born in 1914.
Australian actress LORRAE DESMOND, who began her career as a singing cigarette-girl, was born in 1931.

American singer DON McLEAN, who came from nowhere in 1971 with the hit "American Pie", was born in 1945. He also had hits with "Vincent" (1972), and "Crying" (1980). The 1973 hit by ROBERTA FLACK "Killing Me Softly With His Song" is about DON McLEAN.
British bass player MICHAEL RUTHERFORD, who played with the band 'Genesis' and later formed 'Mike and The Mechanics' (with PAUL CARRACK as lead singer) in 1985, was born in 1950.

British bass player, singer and songwriter STING (GORDON SUMNER) was born in 1951. His nickname came from his liking for black and yellow striped jumpers, and dates back to the early 1970s. He formed 'Police' in 1977, and the band began a run of hits from 1979 including "Can't Stand Losing You", "Message In A Bottle", "Walking On The Moon", and later - "Don't Stand So Close To Me" (1980), "Every Breath You Take" (1983).
** EVENTS **
322BC: Greek philosopher ARISTOTLE died of a stomach
illness.
1803 : American statesman SAMUEL ADAMS died. He was one
of the signatories on the American Declaration of Independence.
1913 : The flagship of the Australian Navy, Invincible
Class battle cruiser 'HMAS AUSTRALIA', sailed into its home port of Jervis Bay in New South Wales.
1913 : An "Aero-bus" biplane set a new record by carrying
ten people, including the pilot, during a flight at H*ndon in England.
1919 : Paris ratified the Versailles Peace Treaty, which
ended World War I and established the League of Nations.
1920 : Richmond won their first Victorian Football League
(VFL) premiership, defeating Collingwood at the MCG, 7.10-52 to 5.5-35.
1922 : The elusive LESLIE "Squizzy" TAYLOR, linked to

Melbourne's criminal underworld, was shot at three times and wounded in Bourke Street in the city. He had surrendered to police only days earlier, after eluding authorities for a year on charges of breaking into a city bond store.
1925 : London's first red double-decker buses began
services.
1930 : The Australian federal cabinet recommended that
MP's and public servants should take a salary cut.
1931 : Tea tycoon and yachtsman SIR THOMAS LIPTON died in
London at the age of 81. The one success that eluded this enormously successful man was victory in the prestigious America's Cup yacht race.
1935 : Rolls-Royce announced the production of its new
50-horsepower, 12-cylinder "Phantom III", costing 1,850-pounds.
1942 : Millions of tons of food were canned and stored in
central Australia, under a government plan, preparing for the evacuation of the population to inland regions should coastal areas come under attack during World War II.
1950 : A new cartoon strip by CHARLES.M.SCHULTZ was
published, called "Peanuts" and featuring characters such as CHARLIE BROWN and SNOOPY.
1954 : A nine-power conference admitted West Germany to
NATO, but without its own nuclear arms.
1958 : Farmers on the eastern coast of both New Zealand
islands faced their worst drought in 40 years.
1959 : The ferry "Princess of Tasmania" began services
between Melbourne and Devonport.
1970 : Three hundred boys at Melbourne's Mordialloc High
School refused to return to class, after 50 fellow students were sent home because their hair was too long.
1979 : Yorkshire Police launched a one-million pound
publicity campaign, in a bid to find the "Yorkshire Ripper".
1985 : American film actor ROCK HUDSON, promoted by

Hollywood as the All-American boy in the 1950's, died of AIDS at his Beverly Hills mansion. HUDSON told the world ten months earlier that he had contracted the disease, after spending two years denying his illness and refusing to believe it would prove fatal. He was born on the 17th of November, 1925.
1987 : British biologist SIR PETER MEDAWAR died. He won a
Nobel Prize for his work on skin-grafting.
1994 : Nine people died when their light plane ditched
into the sea while flying to Lord Howe Island.
